e.etymology: Italian short form of Giovanna, the feminine of Giovanni (John), from Hebrew Yochanan, 'God is gracious'. US use jumped in 2020 after the death of Gianna Bryant.
namesakes: Saint Gianna Beretta Molla (Italian physician and saint)

e.etymology: From two surnames: English Ryley, 'rye clearing', from Old English ryge plus leah, and Irish Reilly, from O Raghallaigh, 'descendant of Raghallach'. Once a boys' name, it now goes mostly to girls.

assoc.t: Riley, the girl in Pixar's Inside Out
the life of Riley, an easy and carefree life

e.etymology: From an English surname for a dyer or seller of scarlet, a fine cloth. Margaret Mitchell's Scarlett O'Hara in Gone with the Wind (1936) turned it into a first name.

assoc.t: Scarlett O'Hara of Gone with the Wind
scarlet, the bright red color
Miss Scarlet in the board game Clue

e.etymology: From Latin aurora, 'dawn', and the Roman goddess of the dawn. The northern and southern lights are named for her.

assoc.t: Princess Aurora, Disney's Sleeping Beauty
aurora borealis, the northern lights
Aurora, Colorado, and Aurora, Illinois

e.etymology: From Greek khloe, 'young green shoot', a title of the goddess Demeter. A Chloe is mentioned once in the New Testament, and the name stars in the Greek romance Daphnis and Chloe.
namesakes: Khloe Kardashian (reality TV star, spelled Khloe)

assoc.t: Chloe, the French fashion and perfume house

e.etymology: From the English word for the hazel tree and its light brown color, from Old English haesel. One of the plant names given to girls from the late 1800s.
namesakes: Hazel Grace Lancaster (The Fault in Our Stars heroine)

assoc.t: hazel, the green-brown eye color, and the hazelnut tree

e.meaning: air; a solo song in opera
e.etymology: From the Italian word aria, 'air', used for a solo song in opera. It took off in the 2010s alongside Aria of Pretty Little Liars and Arya of Game of Thrones. Similar names exist in Persian, Hebrew and Sanskrit.
namesakes: Arya Stark (Game of Thrones character, spelled Arya)

assoc.t: aria, a solo song in an opera
Aria Resort and Casino on the Las Vegas Strip

e.meaning: short form of Honora (honor) or Eleanor
e.etymology: A short form of Honora, from Latin honor, and of Eleanor. It took root in Ireland and became known worldwide through Nora, the heroine of Ibsen's play A Doll's House.
namesakes: Nora Ephron (writer and director of Sleepless in Seattle)

e.meaning: uncertain; perhaps weaver, or a kind of duck
e.etymology: From Greek Penelope, perhaps from penelops, a kind of duck, or from pene, 'thread'. In Homer's Odyssey she is the faithful wife who weaves by day and unravels by night while she waits for Odysseus.
namesakes: Penelope (wife of Odysseus in the Odyssey)

assoc.t: Penelope, faithful wife of Odysseus in the Odyssey

e.etymology: From the English occupational surname for the keeper of a park or game preserve.

assoc.t: Peter Parker, Spider-Man's alter ego (surname)
Parker pens

e.etymology: English form of Latin Aemilia, the feminine of the Roman family name Aemilius, from aemulus, 'rival'. It was the top US girls' name from 1996 to 2007.
From the Norman French name Milo, of uncertain origin, possibly Germanic or from Slavic mil, 'gracious'. English speakers long linked it with Latin miles, 'soldier'.
namesakes: Miles Morales (Spider-Man of Into the Spider-Verse)

assoc.t: miles, the unit of distance, and airline miles

e.etymology: From the English name of the flower, from Latin lilium, a symbol of purity in Christian art. Also a pet form of Lillian and Elizabeth.

assoc.t: lily, the flower

e.meaning: short form of Eleanor, Ellen and names ending in -ella
e.etymology: A 19th-century shortening of Eleanor and Ellen, later of names such as Gabriella and Isabella. An older Norman name Ella came from the Germanic element ali, 'other'.
namesakes: Ella of Frell (heroine of Ella Enchanted)

e.meaning: pet form of Eleanor, Ellen, Elizabeth and other El- names
e.etymology: A pet form of Eleanor, Ellen, Elizabeth, Elena and other names beginning with El-, now given as a name in its own right.
namesakes: Ellie (heroine of The Last of Us)

assoc.t: Ellie, heroine of The Last of Us games and HBO series

e.etymology: From the English occupational surname for a maker of wooden barrels and casks.

assoc.t: Mini Cooper car
Cooper Tires

e.note: Also one of the most popular dog names in the US.

e.etymology: From Hebrew Avigayil, 'my father's joy'. In the Old Testament she is the wise wife of King David. English Puritans took the name up in the 16th century.
namesakes: Abigail Adams (first lady, wife of John Adams)
Abigail Van Buren (pen name of the Dear Abby columnist)

e.etymology: Coined in the United States in the late 20th century, joining the initial J to the sound of Aidan, Braden, Caden and Hayden. It has gone to both boys and girls from the start.
namesakes: Jaden Smith (actor and musician, spelled Jaden)
e.note: Part of the 2000s wave of rhyming -ayden names (Aiden, Brayden, Kayden), so classrooms may hold several.

e.etymology: From Hebrew Eli'ana: El, 'God', plus -i, 'my', plus ana, 'answered'. The Italian, Spanish and Portuguese Eliana is a separate name, a form of French Eliane, from the Roman family name Aelianus.
A Slavic short form of names with the element mil, 'gracious, dear', such as Ludmila and Milena. In Spanish it is also short for Milagros, 'miracles'.
From French Charles, from Latin Carolus and Germanic karl, 'free man'. Charlemagne, Charles the Great, made it a royal name across Europe.
From Arabic Layla, 'night'. She is the beloved in the old Arabic love story of Layla and Majnun, which inspired Eric Clapton's 1970 song Layla.

assoc.t: Layla, the 1970 Eric Clapton rock song

e.etymology: From Hebrew Yoshiyahu, read as 'Yahweh supports' or 'Yahweh has healed'. Josiah became king of Judah at the age of eight and is remembered for his religious reforms.
namesakes: Josiah (boy king of Judah in the Old Testament)
Josiah Bartlet (president in The West Wing)

e.etymology: From Hebrew Kalev, possibly related to kelev, 'dog', an image of devotion, and often read as 'whole-hearted'. Caleb was one of the two faithful spies Moses sent into Canaan. Puritans took the name up.
namesakes: Caleb (Old Testament spy and companion of Joshua)

e.etymology: From Hebrew Yechezkel, 'God strengthens'. The prophet of the Babylonian exile, whose visions include the valley of dry bones.

assoc.t: Ezekiel bread, sprouted-grain loaf named for a Bible verse

e.etymology: From Irish Ruadhan, 'little red one', a saint's name, and the surname O Ruadhain. Many also link it to the rowan tree and its red berries.

assoc.t: rowan, the mountain ash tree with red berries

e.etymology: From Latin nova, 'new'. In astronomy a nova is a star that suddenly flares in brightness. The name has been used in the US since the 1800s.

assoc.t: nova, a star that suddenly brightens
NOVA, the long-running PBS science series
Chevrolet Nova, compact car of the 1960s and 70s

e.note: In Spanish, no va means it doesn't go, the root of an old joke about the Chevy Nova.

e.etymology: From Islay, an island off the west coast of Scotland; two Scottish rivers are also called Isla. The root of the place name is unknown. The same spelling is the Spanish word for island.

assoc.t: isla, the Spanish word for island

e.note: The s is silent (EYE-luh). Expect mispronunciations; Spanish speakers read it as EEZ-lah, their word for island.

e.etymology: From the Scottish Highland clan name Cameron, from Gaelic cam, 'crooked', plus sron, 'nose'.
namesakes: James Cameron (Titanic and Avatar director; surname)

e.etymology: From medieval Latin Angelus, from Greek angelos, 'messenger'. Most American boys named Angel carry the Spanish name, said AHN-hel; English speakers give it to both boys and girls.
namesakes: Angel (vampire hero of Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Angel)

assoc.t: angel, a heavenly being and a term of endearment

e.note: English speakers often hear Angel as a girls' name; in Spanish it is a long-established boys' name.

e.etymology: From the English city of Lincoln, Roman Lindum Colonia: a Celtic word for 'pool' plus Latin colonia, 'settlement'. Americans first gave it as a first name in honor of Abraham Lincoln.

assoc.t: President Abraham Lincoln (surname)
Lincoln, Ford's luxury car brand
Lincoln, capital of Nebraska
Lincoln Logs, notched wooden building toy

e.etymology: From Hebrew Yeshayahu, 'Yahweh is salvation'. The major Old Testament prophet whose book is among the most quoted in the New Testament.
namesakes: Isiah Thomas (basketball Hall of Famer, spelled Isiah)
